findings.text: RCU stall monitoring exposes tunable globals covering normal grace period timeout, expedited timeout, warning suppression for steady state and boot, and an option to include blocked-task details for expedited stalls. All are annotated for mostly-read access.
A nonzero suppress value means stall warnings are suppressed, with a distinct boot-phase control; timeout tunables start from build-time stall timeout settings.
A query helper reports the completed-state cookie used by polling-style synchronize interfaces, always indicating completion.
Early-boot deferred release uses a small wrapper holding an RCU callback head, paired with a saved SRCU cookie variable retained across early initialization.

Early-boot self verification is gated on a self-test flag and exercises an RCU barrier stage plus an SRCU barrier stage, then polls the saved SRCU cookie expecting success and releases the early SRCU instance before evaluating the callback counter for a pass or fail status.

The self-test callback increments a global execution counter and emits an informational message; the verifier treats agreement between that counter and the number of exercised barrier stages as the pass criterion.

A mismatch between expected and observed self-test callbacks triggers a warning and a negative status, while a failed SRCU completion poll triggers a once-only warning without changing the counted stages.
